core.title: Declare every theme in the repository's theme registry
core.given: A plan has a repository-owned theme registry and/or plan artifacts carrying a theme (new, changed, or unchanged); registry-only work included.
core.when: The planner authors, edits, or validates a themed plan artifact or the theme registry.
core.then: Every theme on every themed plan artifact MUST resolve to a value in the repository-owned theme registry.
prefer: Declare themes in the repository's theme registry with any kebab-case name.
Keep the registry's first position reserved for commons: if the first position is populated, its name is commons.
Treat an unresolved theme as a plan error; fix the registry or the artifact.
Check all of: the first registry position, if populated, is commons; names are kebab-case; every artifact theme resolves. Resolution alone is not compliance.
avoid: Relying on a default taxonomy supplied by the toolkit or package; none exists, and no game or toolkit vocabulary is provided.
Expecting a package-default lookup to resolve an undeclared theme.
Any name other than commons in the registry's first position.
core.why: Themes are repository-owned with no package fallback, so an undeclared theme is a plan error. Downstream naming and boundary rules presuppose a resolvable theme.
evidence: Every theme on every themed plan artifact (new or existing) appears as a value in the theme registry (canonical resolution).
In the theme registry, the first position, if populated, is commons, and all names are kebab-case; checked even when no artifact changed and all references resolve.
The stack's plan static validator reports no findings for this rule.
verification: Canonical resolution: a theme resolves when it equals a value in the repository-owned theme registry. The registry is the only source of theme names (package defaults: none); each consuming repository declares its own names.
Do not fall back to any package-default theme list; an undeclared theme is a plan error, not a package-default lookup.
Scope: themes on all themed plan artifacts in the plan, not only changed ones.

Registry names: any kebab-case name, except the first position is reserved for commons. Reservation semantics: a finding only when the first position is populated with a name other than commons; do not require that the first position be populated or that a commons entry exist; evaluate the resulting registry after reorders rather than flagging the move itself. Check registry shape independently of reference resolution.
Enforced by the stack's plan static validator; the concrete validator, finding, and term ids are realization details.

values: registry entry added, renamed, reordered, or removed
registry first position populated with a name other than commons

fires: A planner authors a new plan artifact of a themed kind and sets its theme.
A planner changes the theme of an existing plan artifact.
A planner renames or removes an entry in the theme registry that artifacts still reference.
The plan is validated and an existing, unchanged artifact references a theme not declared in the theme registry.
A plan uses a theme name assumed to come from a default taxonomy that is not declared in the theme registry.
A planner edits or validates the theme registry (even with no themed artifact touched) and the registry contains a non-kebab-case name.

A planner edits or validates the theme registry and its first position is populated with a name other than commons (e.g. after reordering, the resulting registry has another name in the first position).
Every artifact theme resolves, but the registry itself violates the kebab-case naming rule or the first-position reservation for commons.
doesNotFire: Plan validation or edits where every theme on every themed plan artifact resolves to a value in the theme registry, all registry names are kebab-case, and the first position is either commons or unpopulated.
Changes that touch no file under the plan root (recursively: nothing anywhere below the root path of plan artifacts) and neither touch the theme registry nor reference any plan-artifact theme.
Adding a new kebab-case theme to the registry outside the first position, with the first position untouched and no artifact referencing an undeclared theme.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that carry a theme field (plus the registry kind itself), which instantiate 'themed plan artifact' in the core.
Path of the repository-owned theme registry that every theme must resolve against (proposed key; no existing key names it).

Root path of plan artifacts (the plan tree): themed plan artifacts and the theme registry live under this root. The core activation derives its recursive scope — every file anywhere under this root — from this path; the value is a root path, not a glob.

bunOnly.text: The planner static validator (planner.static.validators.bun) reports no planner.theme.must-be-canonical findings.
bunOnly.reason: Validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details; the core's evidence names the check generically.

bunOnly.text: Term id canonical_resolution; values: source=plan/_themes.yaml; package_defaults=none; consumer_repo=declares its own names.
bunOnly.reason: The term id is a realization identifier and the registry path is profile data; the core keeps the resolution semantics in verification without the identifier.

bunOnly.text: Findings prefixed planner.theme.must-be-canonical (unresolved theme reference; non-kebab-case registry name; index 0 occupied by a name other than commons) from the planner static validator (planner.static.validators.bun) or a registry-shape observer that parses plan/_themes.yaml.
bunOnly.reason: Finding ids and the validator ref are realization details; the core's finding fact lists the neutral finding descriptions.

The path_glob 'plan/**' is the recursive scope over the plan root: roots.plan holds the root path 'plan' (a path, not a glob), and the core activation derives descendant scope from that root (doesNotFire: 'no file under the plan root, recursively'), realized as the file_kind fact over the plan_artifact and theme_registry kinds that live under it. 'plan/_themes.yaml' is the theme registry path (layout.registries#theme_registry).

neutralityNotes: The theme-registry format itself (an ordered list of kebab-case names whose first position is reserved for commons) is treated as plan-schema content rather than stack machinery: kebab-case and commons name no stack, runtime, framework, language or path, and commons is a cross-stack plan concept (cf. layout.commons_dir), so both stay in the core; 'index 0' is reworded as 'first position'. The concrete registry path, the plan root and the themed artifact kinds come from the profile: roots.plan carries the root path 'plan' as a path (not the 'plan/**' glob), and the core activation derives the recursive everything-under-that-root scope from it; no existing vocabulary key names the theme registry, so layout.registries#theme_registry is proposed. Validator, finding and term ids (planner.static.validators.bun, planner.theme.must-be-canonical findings, canonical_resolution) are bunOnly; per-rule severity and disposition stay in core verification. 'The planner' is kept as the plan-authoring role.
